Every prayer flag in the Himalaya is a prayer for everyone who passes beneath it. 🙏

The five colours are never random. In Tibetan Buddhist tradition:
🔵 Blue is the sky and space
⚪ White is the air and wind
🔴 Red is fire
🟢 Green is water
🟡 Yellow is earth

The belief is that the wind carries the prayers and mantras printed on them out into the world, spreading goodwill and compassion to all. As the flags fade in the sun and wind, the prayers are said to become part of the universe.

On our treks in the Everest, Langtang and Annapurna regions you will walk under thousands of them, private to your group, with a guide who can tell you what they say.

Two old royal cities of the Kathmandu Valley, a short drive apart. You have one free morning: which one? 🛕

🅰️ Patan (Lalitpur), the city of artisans. Its Durbar Square is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and its craftsmen still work metal in the old repoussé and lost-wax ways. The Krishna Temple, with its 21 gilded spires, was built in 1637.

🅱️ Bhaktapur, whose old name Bhadgaon means the City of Devotees. It is home to the five-storey Nyatapola temple and is famous for its pottery and woodcarving.

Our 3-day Kathmandu Heritage & Culture trip includes both: Patan on Day 2, Bhaktapur on Day 3, all entry fees included, with a private vehicle and an experienced guide.

Five small things that show respect at any temple in Nepal. 🙏 Save this for your trip.

👟 Shoes come off before you step into a temple or shrine
👜 Leather is not allowed inside some temple areas, so leave the belt and bag with your guide
🔁 Walk around temples and stupas clockwise, keeping them on your right
📷 Ask before photographing people, rituals or shrines
🛕 Some Hindu temples do not allow non-Hindus inside. At Pashupatinath, for example, the inner temple is for Hindus only

On every private tour, our guides walk you through the customs of each temple before you go in, so you never have to guess.
